pattern_judgments.rationale: The candidate has one supporting workflow and one repository, with no mandatory action or cross-repository equivalent-action cluster. Its contract-alignment action and generated-fixture validation action are complementary stages of the same openai/codex workflow, not independent support for a reusable pattern.
missing_probes: Add an independent repository workflow whose mandatory repair aligns a versioned or generated client contract with its producer using the same parseability and field-preservation postcondition.
Add a runtime consumer probe that parses the corrected discriminator variants and verifies preserved payload fields, in addition to generated-fixture comparison.

pattern_judgments.rationale: The workflows span three repositories, but their mandatory mechanisms do not align: Hermes establishes and fences a durable conversation lease, pi reconciles deferred tool calls after a preflight abort, and gemini-cli partitions pending session-context history. Their postconditions and validation oracles are different, so repository count alone does not establish a reusable coordination action.
missing_probes: Find an independent repository implementing the same atomic conversation-admission and stale-holder-fencing action, and test contention, expiry or reclamation, holder-qualified cleanup, and coherent post-admission reload.
Alternatively, establish an explicit cross-repository cancellation-gate cluster with the same no-side-effect and recorded-error-result postcondition and matching event/result oracle.
Probe behavior when ownership is lost during active work and when multiple operating-system processes, rather than separate database handles in one process, contend for the same conversation.

pattern_judgments.rationale: Only one openai/codex workflow supports this candidate. The Unix descriptor-boundary guard and its integration validation are an implementation/validation pair within that repository, with no independent repository demonstrating the same stdio-only inheritance postcondition and descendant-process oracle.
missing_probes: Add an independent repository workflow that enforces a comparable local extension-process resource boundary while preserving the explicit transport and launch contract.

Probe both the server and a descendant for exclusion of unrelated inherited descriptors or handles, while also checking transport round trips, launch variants, parent ownership, and exec-failure behavior.

pattern_judgments.rationale: Seven workflows across four repositories are grouped under this broad category, but their actions are not equivalent: Qwen's all-or-none deferred-schema preload, Aider's request-local one-token cache warming, Hermes's proportional compression default and migration, and gemini-cli's nudges, rollback, request normalization, and edit guards have different mechanisms, postconditions, and validation oracles. No mandatory cross-repository action cluster is supported.
missing_probes: Identify at least two independent repositories implementing the same bounded-resource operation, such as a temporary maintenance cap that preserves the normal request budget, and require matching maintenance/normal-path assertions.
For a preload-style cluster, obtain an independent workflow with the same combined-footprint all-or-none reveal postcondition and fit/overflow oracle.
Probe zero, invalid, and over-budget inputs together with the ordinary path to verify that the bound prevents excess work without changing normal behavior.

unresolved: No action pair satisfies the strict merge requirement of the same reusable operation, semantic level, meaningful postcondition, and validation oracle; the closest same-episode or same-workflow pairs are distinct implementation stages, predicate branches, or validation companions.
All pattern candidates lack an untouched holdout end-task result, and none has sufficient independent cross-repository support for promotion.
